simple.meaning: חֵזִיר (Chêzîyr) is a Hebrew word meaning “Chezir , the name of two Israelites.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: חֵזִיר (H2387) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at 1 Chronicles 24:15, with occurrences in 1 Chronicles, Nehemiah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to חֵזִיר (H2387) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in חֵזִיר (H2387) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: חֵזִיר (Chêzîyr) / H2387 is traced through 1 Chronicles 24:15, Nehemiah 10:21 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

Chezir חֵזִיר proper name, masculine (compare inscription in RA 1867, plural 7 , Dr Sm xxiii ; Nö ZMG 1886, 162 'pointing — ֵ֯ to avoid offence;' but Nbr Acad. 1887, Dec. 17 compare Talmud & ᵑ7 ( חֲזוּרָא חֵיזוּר, חַזּוּרָא, etc.) pomegranate (and apple ; Syriac , ), compare רִמּוֺן בְּנֵי 2Sam 4:2 , 5 , 9 ) — 1 a priest of 17th course (assigned to David's time) 1Chr 24:15 ; ᵐ5 Χηξειν (16th, 24:14 ), but A Ιεξειρ, ᵐ5 L Χηξειρ. 2 one of those sealed Neh 10:21 ; ᵐ5 Ηξειρ, ᵐ5 L Αξηρ.
